Novel element: Read-only guidance - the system never injects input
What it is (plain language): The client only displays the next instruction; it never sends a click, keystroke, command, or form submission into the application you are using. You perform every action yourself, so the human stays accountable for every change.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): Agentic / RPA assistants (Verizon US 2025/0238087, Apple US 12,406,664, Vasylyev US 2024/0412720) act for the user, and even the closest guided-help art (USAA US 11,989,786 and US 12,346,977) recites a system that "automatically assists." No verified reference claims a screen-grounded assistant structurally barred from injecting input, with the human's own action as the only state change.

Novel element: Observe -> instruct -> verify -> correct -> advance loop grounded in real-time screen state
What it is (plain language): The plan moves to the next step only after a later captured frame actually shows the expected result; a wrong move produces a corrective instruction instead of advancing.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): Prior guided-help (Boomersurf US 10,852,898; USAA US 11,989,786 / US 12,346,977; Meta US 11,036,984; Visautact US 10,290,222) gates on GUI-object/accessibility data, camera/AR input, or pre-authored tutorials - not vision over a screenshot of an arbitrary application used as the verification oracle.

Novel element: Visible-when-done condition on every plan step
What it is (plain language): The model-generated checklist attaches to each step a description of exactly what will be on screen when that step is truly finished, so completion is read from the display rather than assumed.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): Prior art relies on pre-authored step images or sensed micro-steps. No verified reference pairs a model-generated plan for an arbitrary user-stated goal with a per-step visible-when-done test evaluated from a redacted screenshot.

What it is (plain language): For each frame the vision model returns a single record: completed steps, the one current step, one screen-specific micro-action, a one-line observation, a problem flag, and a done flag.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): No verified reference defines this specific completed / current / guidance / observation / flag / done contract, exchanged once per frame, as the control structure for guidance the human then performs.

Novel element: Proactive prerequisite insertion and UI-drift re-targeting
What it is (plain language): If something the current step needs is missing on screen, the guidance switches to establishing it first; if a named control has moved or been renamed since planning, the guidance points to the equivalent visible control and states that the interface differs.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): Pre-authored walkthroughs (Boomersurf; WalkMe-class digital adoption platforms) break when the UI drifts or a prerequisite is absent; they cannot re-target to an equivalent control seen in a live frame or insert a missing prerequisite on the fly.

Novel element: On-device OCR frame redaction before any frame is transmitted
What it is (plain language): Before a frame leaves the device, on-device OCR reads each text line and the same policy engine used for typed text masks every line holding sensitive data; the masked image is what is sent.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): Capital One US 12,013,965 masks only its own application's known GUI fields; JPMorgan US 2025/0005060, IBM US 2025/0086310 and others redact at a server/gateway. None OCRs an arbitrary third-party app's frame on-device using the identical DLP engine (including tenant block-words and custom patterns) as the text path.

Novel element: Fail-safe downscale backstop when OCR is unavailable
What it is (plain language): If the on-device OCR engine cannot run, the frame is heavily downscaled so fine text is illegible rather than transmitted at full resolution - a safe default, honestly reported as a best-effort backstop.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): No verified redaction reference describes a legibility-destroying downscale fallback that prevents full-resolution leakage when the on-device recognizer fails to load or run.

Novel element: Reversible, device-only tokenization with a volatile token map
What it is (plain language): Sensitive values in outbound text are replaced with stable typed placeholders (for example [[EMAIL_1]], [[IP_2]]); the token-to-value map lives only in device memory, is never transmitted or written to any server log, and is discarded when the session ends.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): Capital One US 2024/0111891 sanitizes irreversibly; JPMorgan US 2025/0005060 and IBM US 2025/0086310 mask at a server / moderator with no restoration. No verified reference keeps a reversible mapping device-only for later local restoration in a screen-guidance client.

Novel element: Local rehydration of the model's answer, including streaming
What it is (plain language): Placeholders in the model's reply are swapped back to the real values on the device - applied to each streamed chunk as it arrives - so the user reads a complete answer that the server and the model never saw.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): Server- and moderator-side masking art does not restore the originals in the response at all. No verified reference performs on-device, streaming rehydration of a model answer whose sensitive values never left the device.

Novel element: Never-guess fallback for a missing or garbled token
What it is (plain language): If a placeholder is missing or altered in the reply, the text is left as the placeholder and flagged incomplete at that point - the system never invents or substitutes a value not in the token map.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): Reversible-masking schemes do not describe an explicit no-fabrication rule that leaves and flags the placeholder rather than guessing a value, protecting against silent corruption of the restored answer.

What it is (plain language): Every command or code block in a plan is matched against a catalog of destructive patterns and flagged (hidden behind an explicit acknowledgment), and named dependency versions are checked against a vulnerability database before the user is shown them.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): Guided-help and agentic art do not add a deterministic safety gate over the exact commands and code handed to a human, with a report-rather-than-silently-pass behaviour when the vulnerability source is unreachable.

Novel element: Evidence captured only on verification, reusing the already-redacted frame
What it is (plain language): When a step is first verified, the frame already redacted for transmission is kept as that step's evidence - once per step, encrypted at rest - so nothing additional ever leaves the device to build the record.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): Screen-recording / DLP art captures a separate recording. No verified reference ties evidence capture to the verification event and reuses the same already-redacted frame, adding zero additional egress.

Novel element: Tenant-enforced egress policy including the screenshot-evidence retention switch
What it is (plain language): A per-company policy object (per-category send / redact / withhold / tokenize, block-words, mode, a switch for whether redacted evidence frames are kept at all, a retention window, armed/locked) is pushed to member devices and enforced there; members cannot weaken it and the server re-applies it as defense in depth.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): General cloud / endpoint DLP exists, but no verified reference binds a per-tenant policy object - including an on/off switch for retaining screenshot evidence - to on-device enforcement inside an AI screen-guidance client with arm and lock semantics a member cannot override.

Novel element: Audit log recording each redacted transmission by counts, not the removed values
What it is (plain language): Every transmission is logged with the policy version in force, the mode, counts of what was removed per category, and whether a frame was sent - never the removed values; a sweep then deletes each expired session together with its evidence frames and its audit log in one operation.
Why it is novel (vs the prior art found): No verified reference records a per-transmission audit that deliberately stores counts rather than the sensitive values, coupled to a single-operation retention sweep of the session, its evidence, and its log together.
